description: Olá! Sou o Wisley, apaixonado por tecnologia e espaço. Tenho experiência em Design UI/UX e Front-end. Estamos a criar uma ferramenta web para comparar locais e datas de pouso no polo sul da Lua, visualizando o Sol e a Terra para energia e comunicação. Junta-te a nós!
summary: LunaSight helps mission planners, educators, and the public understand how an arrival delay can change a lunar landing plan. It compares candidate sites across original and delayed mission windows, showing direct sunlight, the longest continuous period of darkness, and Earth line of sight against local terrain. Users can explore a LOLA-derived terrain map and 3D site views, inspect the Sun and Earth relative to the horizon, and set optional mission requirements. An educational guide explains the calculations, while a configurable suitability score and a rule-based assistant make trade-offs easier to interpret. Sunlight is treated as an environmental input, not guaranteed electrical power; Earth line of sight is not a guaranteed radio link. LunaSight combines NASA JPL Horizons ephemerides with NASA LRO LOLA elevation data to make complex lunar planning information easier to compare.
details:
LunaSight helps users compare lunar landing-site conditions across original and delayed arrival dates. It reports direct-sunlight share, longest continuous darkness, and geometric Earth line of sight over the mission window. A timeline shows the Sun and Earth relative to the local terrain horizon.

Users can explore a LOLA-derived map, 3D terrain, a 30-day solar calendar, and optional mission requirements. The energy panel estimates solar energy per square metre from user-provided panel efficiency and orientation assumptions. The configurable suitability score combines sunlight, darkness, Earth visibility, and terrain slope. A rule-based assistant explains results using the displayed values; team notes remain in the user’s browser.

LunaSight uses NASA JPL Horizons ephemerides and NASA LRO LOLA elevation data. It was built with React, TypeScript, Vite, and Three.js. Sunlight availability is not guaranteed electrical power, the suitability score is a planning aid rather than a NASA rating, and geometric line of sight does not guarantee radio communication.
